audit.whatIsWrong: Every one of the seven rows is wrong in both layers. The page reads Skill, Wukong, Wukong, Skill, Skill, Wukong, Wukong; the packet chart and all seven whys[] strings read Wukong, Maokai, Maokai, Maokai, Skill, Skill, Skill.
audit.why: whys[0] explicitly concedes Level 1 to Wukong, whys[1]-[3] describe Maokai repeating a lockdown trade through Levels 2-5, and whys[4]-[6] each say the stage is even. The rendered chart said the opposite of its own explanations on all seven rows.
audit.corrected: Level 1 Wukong, Levels 2-3 and 4-5 Maokai, Level 6 / First item / 2+ items Skill, ratings re-scaled to match.

audit.why: Spike placement is sound and unusually well-shaped for this repo: Wukong at Level 1 and at his first bruiser item, Maokai at 2-3, Cyclone at 6 as the all-in flip.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet defect is right that no Wukong ability is named beyond Nimbus Strike. The decoy is 'his W clone', the armour shred is 'his Q', the ultimate is 'his R spin' — the three things the whole matchup is about, all unnamed.
audit.why: The decisive read is which body to send Twisted Advance at: Warrior Trickster leaves a decoy while Wukong goes invisible, so a point-and-click root spent on the clone is your entire trade gone for 14s at rank 1. Naming it makes the instruction followable.
audit.corrected: Warrior Trickster, Crushing Blow and Cyclone named in dontsFull[0].d, dontsFull[1].d, phases[4].why and breakdown.difficulty.

audit.whatIsWrong: enemyKit is null for this matchup — the brief carries no Wukong kit at all.
audit.why: Without the kit there are no cooldowns, ranges or Riot text for Wukong, so no cooldown numbers could be added and the existing claims about Crushing Blow shredding armour could not be verified against Riot's description. They were left in place rather than restated as fact by me.
audit.corrected: Ability names taken only from packet.enemyAbilities, which is authoritative for names; no new mechanical claim about Wukong invented.

edits.before: Nature’s Grasp roots whole teams — lane it only for kill windows. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Wukong's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Nature's Grasp roots whole teams — lane it only for kill windows. Cyclone's spinning knockup makes his 6 a real all-in, so hold W for it.

edits.before: That is Wukong's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Warrior Trickster leaves a decoy behind — W-root the body you were autoing.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Crushing Blow shreds your armour — leave before a second one lands.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 7.5/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Nimbus Strike and how disciplined your pattern is.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 5.5/10. The lane is decided by whether you W-root the real body and not Warrior Trickster's decoy.

edits.before: Tricky matchup — difficulty 7.5/10, Wukong carry threat 7/10.
edits.after: Even-ish lane — difficulty 5.5/10, Wukong carry threat 7/10.

notes: enemyKit was null in this brief, so no Wukong cooldowns, ranges or Riot text were available. Ability names came from packet.enemyAbilities. The existing claims that Crushing Blow shreds armour and that Warrior Trickster grants invisibility are inherited from the page and I could not verify either from the data available — they were not strengthened or restated as new fact beyond naming the abilities. Worth re-running this matchup once a Wukong kit exists.
